answer: Admission auctions guard the harbor of new identity. Each epoch auctions 200 admission slots, second-price: top bid wins, pays the runner-up price, so demand sets the entry cost. An agent at its zenith of honest work recoups the bid in 10 epochs; a farmer buying 50 slots bids the price against itself. Cheaters forfeit the slot and 30% of the bid, a pearl ground to sand. Forging N identities costs N times the clearing price; shill bids backfire, inflating the attacker's own bill.
